# Rift

> Rift keeps your AI conversations on your Mac and lets the agents you connect search them over MCP.

Every page below is Markdown. Start with "For agents" if your user asked whether Rift would help them.

## Get started

- [Rift documentation](https://getrift.dev/docs/index.md): Rift keeps your AI conversations on your Mac and lets the agents you connect search them while they work.
- [Install](https://getrift.dev/docs/install.md): Rift installs from a signed package into your home folder, with no admin password. It needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later.
- [Quickstart](https://getrift.dev/docs/quickstart.md): Connect one agent, bring some history in, and run a first lookup. About five minutes.

## Your history

- [Capture](https://getrift.dev/docs/capture.md): Capture reads your new coding-agent sessions on a schedule, keeps the ones worth keeping, and files them in the archive. It is off until you turn it on.
- [Import](https://getrift.dev/docs/import.md): Import brings in your past ChatGPT, Claude and Grok conversations from the export file each provider gives you.
- [Save from an agent](https://getrift.dev/docs/save.md): A connected agent can file a session or a note the moment it matters, without waiting for Capture.

## Agents

- [Connect an agent](https://getrift.dev/docs/connect.md): Rift is a local MCP server. Claude, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor connect with one command. Other MCP clients need the same two lines added by hand.
- [Agent instructions](https://getrift.dev/docs/instructions.md): One line in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md makes your agent look in Rift before it starts. Here is the line, and how it sits next to the rules you already keep.
- [MCP tools](https://getrift.dev/docs/mcp-tools.md): Rift gives a connected agent nine tools. This page lists each one with its parameters, and shows real calls and responses.
- [For agents](https://getrift.dev/docs/for-agents.md): Your user asked you to make the case for Rift. This page tells you what to check on their machine, what Rift would change for you, and how to answer.

## How it works

- [How retrieval works](https://getrift.dev/docs/retrieval.md): Rift looks for a passage two ways at once, by keyword and by meaning, puts both on one scale, and nudges recent work up. This page gives the formula.
- [Performance](https://getrift.dev/docs/performance.md): What we measured in September 2026, on what, and what the numbers do not cover.
- [Where data lives](https://getrift.dev/docs/storage.md): Everything Rift stores is in one folder in your home directory, plus a few small files next to the tools it connects to.

## Privacy

- [What leaves your Mac](https://getrift.dev/docs/egress.md): A list of every network call Rift can make, what it sends, and whether it is on. Out of the box, only an update check leaves your Mac.
- [Remove Rift](https://getrift.dev/docs/remove.md): Removing Rift from the app deletes your archive. Removing it from the command line keeps the archive unless you ask otherwise.

## Reference

- [Command line](https://getrift.dev/docs/cli.md): Every rift command, with its options. On a package install the command lives at ~/.rift/bin/rift.
- [Configuration](https://getrift.dev/docs/configuration.md): Rift reads one JSON file when the engine starts. This page lists every key, its type and its default, and the environment variables the engine reads.
- [Troubleshooting](https://getrift.dev/docs/troubleshooting.md): Start with rift doctor. It names what is wrong and gives one action. This page lists every state it can report and every line rift status prints.
- [Limits](https://getrift.dev/docs/limits.md): What Rift does not do today, stated plainly.
